scope: Review round 1 (independent reviewer, 2026-09-26) found two repository unit tests that the trial's new files fail. Both need a registration in a repository file outside this directory, and simulating them showed a third: manifests/evidence.json hashes the lockfile inventory. This record reproduces the failures, gives the exact entries and records the OSV-Scanner result that the lock registration exposes. No engine ran. No port, manifest, lock, receipt, verdict, run record, scorer or tolerance sheet changed, and nothing was re-scored.
evidence_class: Local integration checks on this host: the repository's own unit tests and the security-scan.yml OSV-Scanner command. The registered state was applied only in a scratch git worktree. It is a simulation of the coordinator's change, not the state of this branch, and not a CI run.

findings.values: the eight mappings[*].decision strings of each arm manifest
findings.class: data. Each string states how one arm maps one LEAN concept onto its engine, like the eight spy-parity manifest strings already listed in DATA_VALUE_SHA256. None states a selection, and blind_checkout.is_label_value returns False for all 16 under the current rules, so registering them changes no blind-checkout output.
findings.why_not_fixed_in_this_directory: The strings are in the frozen arm manifests. Each manifest's sha256 is bound by its receipts and re-verified by compare.py (mapping_manifest_sha256_mismatch). Rewording or re-keying them would unbind every verdict.

registration.digest: sha256 of the exact UTF-8 string, as the test computes it

findings.why_not_fixed_in_this_directory: Each arm manifest binds its lock's path and sha256 (engine.lock), and run.json cites all three. Renaming, untracking or relocking a lock would unbind the manifest from its receipts or change the recorded environment.

registration.precedent: blueprints/us-equities/sim-crosscheck-hftbacktest/requirements.lock, a hashed uv pip compile lock listed with the requirements.txt parser

follow_on_registration.why: scripts/validate.py checks the inventory's sha256 and byte count. With the inventory changed and this entry not, tests.test_catalog_freshness_propose.RebuildExplorerSubprocessTests.test_general_publication_validator_passes_after_the_run failed with '.github/osv-scanner-lockfiles.json: SHA-256 mismatch' and 'byte count mismatch'.

simulated_value.valid_for: the three entries appended to the end of lockfiles and the file rewritten with two-space JSON indentation and a final newline; any other layout has its own value

findings.consequence: Once listed, the required osv-scanner job scans the three locks. ml4t.lock and build.lock are clean. lumibot.lock fails the job on the two advisories under osv_scanner.advisories unless they are ignored. The inventory's excluded list admits only a deliberately vulnerable test fixture. Its decision record (docs/decisions/2026-09-22-github-automation-closure.md) names a second exclusion for a file that is not a test fixture as an overturn condition, so excluding these locks needs an explicit policy decision.

advisories.summary: NLTK: Model-artifact APIs bypass pathsec and touch files outside allowed roots
advisories.precondition: The application enables nltk pathsec enforcement and lets untrusted input choose the model import or export path of TransitionParser.train or parse, AveragedPerceptron.save or load, PerceptronTagger.save_to_json or save_maxent_params.
advisories.reach_in_this_trial: No trial code calls nltk: the ports and probe scripts contain no nltk reference, and neither does any file of the installed lumibot 4.6.1 package (text search). The runs were offline under bwrap with the network unshared and the environment, checkout and LEAN data read-only. Evidence level: source search. Whether a dependency imports nltk at runtime was not traced.
advisories.remedy: none available: the advisory lists no patched release, and the lock is the frozen record of the evaluated environment

advisories.summary: setuptools: MANIFEST.in exclusion bypass in sdist via Unicode normalization collision (NFC/NFD) on macOS APFS/HFS+
advisories.precondition: Building a source distribution whose MANIFEST.in excludes files, on a normalization-preserving file system (macOS APFS or HFS+).
advisories.reach_in_this_trial: Not reached. The environment was installed binary-only on Linux (uv pip sync --require-hashes --no-build), and nothing builds a source distribution with it. The one source build, the ibapi wheel, ran in a separate build environment locked by ibapi-build/build.lock with setuptools 84.0.0, a fixed version, and it built a wheel, not a source distribution.
advisories.remedy: relocking to setuptools 83.0.0 or later would change the frozen record of the evaluated environment, so the lock is not relocked after the run

osv_scanner.ignore_policy: An [[IgnoredVulns]] entry in .github/osv-scanner.toml needs id, a concrete reason and an ignoreUntil at most 90 days after it is added (2026-12-25 for an entry added on 2026-09-26), and is listed with its evidence in docs/decisions/2026-09-22-github-automation-closure.md. The two ids above are enough: OSV-Scanner 2.6.0 filtered each id together with its aliases.
